name: cloud-c3-webserver
description: The phone's local web server, as an APK: a Rust HTTP server compiled natively for Android (static musl, exec'd from nativeLibraryDir) behind a five-tab shell — Pages, API, Home, Files, Configs — whose Pages and API tabs are derived from the server's own route table.
_doc: WHY THERE IS NO ROOTFS ANY MORE. The previous binary was a glibc Node build that bionic cannot load, so the APK carried a proot + glibc rootfs (#288 Route D) to run it. The server is now a Rust crate in server/ that the ship workflow compiles for aarch64-unknown-linux-musl on an arm64 runner (the da_c3-watchdog recipe): a static executable with no PT_INTERP and no DT_NEEDED, the ONE shape the fleet has proven to exec from nativeLibraryDir on a phone (libs:gix, libs:rclone, libs:gh). No rootfs is baked, no loader is mapped, no proot runs, no cross-repo pin is followed: the server and its shell live in this directory and the route table the app's Pages and API tabs render is the server's own (server/src/routes.rs), so a route added there appears in the tabs and a route removed disappears, with no second list anywhere.

server._doc: THE ONE declaration of the binary the APK carries. server/ is the crate; bin_name is its [[bin]]; the ship workflow builds it per ABI with the Rust target named here and hands the result to gradle through C3_WEBSERVER_BIN_DIR/<abi>/<bin_name>; app/build.gradle::stageServer refuses a missing file and a PT_INTERP and lands it as jniLibs/<abi>/<jni_name>; ServerProcess.kt execs applicationInfo.nativeLibraryDir/<jni_name>. The lib*.so name is not decoration: only such a name is extracted to nativeLibraryDir, which is the one place an app may exec from on API 29+.

runtime._doc: Baked into BuildConfig by app/build.gradle and passed to the server positionally as <port> <root>. The server binds 127.0.0.1 only and refuses every other peer.

android._doc_application_id: Identity, not brand (#405/#495): the package id stays through the rename to cloud-c3-webserver, exactly as ac_c3-watchdog keeps com.diegonmarcos.watchdog, because moving it forces a manual reinstall on every phone.
android._doc_target_sdk: 28 for the STORAGE model, no longer for exec. At 28 READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE grants the whole of runtime.serve_root; from 29 scoped storage would need MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE or per-tree grants to serve shared storage. exec is not a reason to stay any more: the server runs from nativeLibraryDir, which is allowed at every targetSdk.

modules._doc: settings.gradle iterates this. One module and no shared library.

toolchain._doc_rust: The server crate builds with the stable channel and no nightly feature; the ship workflow pins it through dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable as da_c3-watchdog does.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps, resolved by build.sh::_resolve_signing from the vault. No fallback key.

release._doc: Per-APK distribution, same data-driven block as every app here; build.sh oras-push and gh-release read it.

variants._doc: supported_abis is exactly the one ABI each APK's binary is built for: an aarch64 static executable cannot start on a 32-bit-only phone.

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds. The Rust crate's own suite (cargo test, including the end-to-end run of the real server) executes in the ship workflow's server job, on the runner that builds the binary.

shell._doc_requires: node runs the shell's pure render block to prove the tabs draw exactly what the route table says. A tester that shells out to a tool which is not installed does not fail, it answers from the tool's absence, so a missing one is fatal at the engine's preflight.
